preamble: Lenition of the voiced postalveolar affricate jīm [dʒ] to the palatal approximant [j] is a classic feature of Eastern Arabian and Gulf dialects of Arabic: Kuwaiti rayyāl 'man' (MSA rajul), diyāy 'chickens' (MSA dajāj), yūʿ 'hunger' (MSA jūʿ). The change is unconditioned, applying word-initially, intervocalically and word-finally, and it is reported for North and South Arabian dialects as well; in the Gulf it is optional and socially marked, and it does not affect recent loans from Modern Standard Arabic.

examples.note: [j] is the contemporary reflex of historical /dʒ/; both variants occur.

sources: al-Qenaie, S. D. (2011). Kuwaiti Arabic: A Socio-Phonological Perspective. Doctoral thesis, Durham University. https://etheses.durham.ac.uk/id/eprint/935/
